title: Deadpool Killed the Avengers. They Weren't His Real Target.
canon: Deadpool Kills the Marvel Universe #1–4 (2012), alternate comic reality Earth-12101.

u3.reason: The disguised doctor and device initiate the failed control attempt.
A new red guiding voice replaces the old thoughts.
Panel boundaries make the new belief legible.

u4.reason: Keep the panel prison visible while his mistaken liberation motive is explained.
Show the stolen size-changing technology and the headquarters attack without graphic injury.

u5.reason: Contrast Hulk’s strength with Wade before the recovery reversal.
Show Wade returning to standing without gore.
Smaller human form and empty green outline explain the vulnerability; omit injury.

u7.reason: Introduce the new guardian and location before opening the route.
Move Wade through the portal at the spoken action.

u9.reason: He reaches toward the viewer after the creator reveal.
The short subscription request follows the final story consequence.

lore_design.reason: Maintain the geometric outline and cutout channel style with material-driven paper, clinic stone, swamp earth and a bright creators room. The red suit stays fixed while backgrounds change for story geography. Trebuchet provides familiar open letter shapes; the dark caption band and quiet lower theater stay separate.

u1.reason: Red costume and target markers establish a threat without revealing the final target.
elements: Deadpool’s mask, swords and belt establish identity.
Shield and armor identify the initial targets; no injury.

u2.reason: Archival paper separates the true source cover from the cold clinical space.
elements: Native-scale checked cover identifies the 2012 collection.
The doctor’s device establishes the failed control attempt.

u3.reason: Muted violet distinguishes the altered inner voice from the physical clinic.
elements: Two old bubbles separate from the new red voice.
Visible panel borders make fiction concrete.

u4.reason: Return to paper as the metaphor becomes the motive driving real story actions.
elements: Strings and the panel frame show perceived control.

u5.reason: Muted stone keeps the physical reversal legible against red and green bodies.
elements: Hulk is larger than Wade; regeneration restores Wade.
Banner is smaller and human; injury remains offscreen.

u6.reason: A page edge becomes a physical obstacle, avoiding another killing montage.
elements: Wade’s hand meets the panel wall.
Marks outside it imply a still-unreached author.

u7.reason: Earthy brown and olive plants establish a swamp; no fire or unrelated particles.
elements: Trees, marsh floor and Man-Thing identify the new location.
Warm gateway rings contrast against earthy material.

u8.reason: Warm working-room light makes the final creators’ space different from cosmic action.
elements: Two generic geometric creators work over a comic layout.
Deadpool enters their room; these are fictional stand-ins, not portraits.

u9.reason: Return to the opening red to complete the shift from heroes to the reader.
elements: Deadpool’s foreground hand crosses the panel.
The subscribe card appears only after the reader reveal.
